title: Gemini for Home has decided ‘Fish Lemon’ is a better name for one owner
summary: The name's Lemon, Fish Lemon.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR One Google Home user says Gemini started calling them “Fish Lemon” after a conversation about cooking fish. The nickname now appears in reminders and on their smart display, and attempts to change it only seem to work temporarily. Other Reddit users in the thread aren’t offering much sympathy. Gemini for Home is supposed to get to know you better over time, but giving you an unwanted pet name might be going a bit too far. After a conversation about cooking fish, one user’s Google Home apparently decided they should henceforth be known as “Fish Lemon.” Funny as it was, the joke has worn a bit thin for the user now, as Gemini seemingly refuses to forget it. In a post on the r/googlehome subreddit , user nynexman4464 explains that the strange nickname appeared a few weeks ago. They remember asking a cooking question involving fish when Google Home responded with something along the lines of, “OK, from now on I’ll call you fish lemon.” They laughed it off at the time, but Fish Lemon has apparently stuck around.

title: Rising Over Louisiana
summary: On Aug. 28, 2026 (the evening of Aug. 27 in some time zones), the Moon passed into Earth’s shadow, creating a deep partial lunar eclipse. At the moment of greatest eclipse, 12:13 a.m. EDT, 96.3% of the Moon’s disk was immersed in Earth’s umbra—the central, darkest part of the shadow where sunlight …
body: A partial lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana on Aug. 28, 2026 NASA/Eric Bordelon On Aug. 28, 2026 (the evening of Aug. 27 in some time zones), the Moon passed into Earth’s shadow, creating a deep partial lunar eclipse . At the moment of greatest eclipse, 12:13 a.m. EDT, 96.3% of the Moon’s disk was immersed in Earth’s umbra—the central, darkest part of the shadow where sunlight is completely blocked. This stage of the eclipse was visible across much of the Americas (except Alaska and northwestern Canada), as well as western Europe and western Africa. This image of the eclipse was captured in southern Louisiana, home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility —the nation’s premier site for manufacturing and assembling large-scale space structures and systems, including the core stages of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket powering the Artemis program.

summary: Are you having problems with Microsoft 365?
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Users are running into issues with Microsoft 365. Microsoft has confirmed that the service is experiencing degradation The problem is affecting OneDrive, SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, and more. Microsoft is currently dealing with an issue affecting its 365 services. So, if you have been experiencing problems with OneDrive, Outlook, and more, you’re not alone. The tech giant has confirmed on its status site that Microsoft 365 is going through service degradation. It appears the impact of the outage extends to several of Microsoft’s offerings, including Universal Print, Outlook for Android and iOS, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Copilot, and more. The issues also vary depending on the service, such as delays or failures to send or receive emails; being unable to load or refresh portions of OneDrive and SharePoint; being unable to create, upload, or retrieve print jobs, and so on.

body: TL;DR YouTube’s new companion experience lets your phone automatically recognize what’s playing on your TV when both devices use the same account. You can use your phone to comment, subscribe, browse, search, and even scroll through Shorts without interrupting the video playing on your TV. You can also send videos from your phone directly to the TV, and the two devices don’t need to be on the same Wi-Fi network. Watching YouTube on a TV is great, but interacting with anything on the screen is a different story. Maybe you want to leave a comment, subscribe to the channel, read the description, or figure out what to watch next. Suddenly, you’re pecking away at an on-screen keyboard with a TV remote, and the phone sitting comfortably in your hand starts looking like the much better option. That’s exactly the problem YouTube is trying to solve with its latest update . The company is giving its TV and mobile apps a much tighter connection, effectively turning your phone into a companion for whatever is playing on the big screen. Better still, setup is minimal. Your phone and TV don’t even need to be on the same Wi-Fi network. As long as you’re signed into the same YouTube account on bo…

title: Acer’s new ePaper monitor could make long work sessions easier on the eyes
summary: The EP130K brings a paper-like display, touch, and high resolution to a portable monitor for long work sessions.
body: TL;DR Acer has unveiled the EP130K ePaper monitor at its IFA 2026 showcase. It features a touch-enabled display with up to 3,200 x 2,400 resolution and a 60Hz refresh rate. The monitor supports color and black-and-white modes and can retain an image without power. ePaper displays have traditionally been associated with e-readers , but the technology is increasingly finding its way into larger displays designed for work and productivity. Acer is joining that trend at IFA 2026 with the new EP130K ePaper monitor, which is aimed at professionals, avid readers, and mobile users who spend long periods working on a screen. The EP130K combines paper-like visuals with a glare-free viewing experience, making it particularly suited to reading and deep work. That paper-like experience is also one of the main reasons ePaper remains appealing for long reading sessions, where the distraction-free presentation can be preferable to a conventional display. The screen also supports touch input, so you can interact with content using a stylus or your finger for writing and drawing.

Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 has been leaked and rumored several times over the last few weeks. Even though the series is several months away from launch, several leaks suggest a major direction change Samsung may be planning for the next flagship lineup. These changes include an i Phone-inspired design for the camera island , though these changes could be limited to the Galaxy S27 Ultra and the new Pro variant . While the vanilla and Plus models remain on the roster, Samsung may march forth with small upgrades only , and new information doesn’t contradict this notion. The charging speeds of the Galaxy S27 and the Galaxy S27 Plus have been listed on China’s 3C approval registry (via tipster Abhishek Yadav on X ). According to this leak, the shorter Galaxy S27 will maintain a peak wired charging speed of 25W, while the taller Galaxy S27 Plus could support charging only up to 45W.

title: YouTube TV just finished rolling out one of its biggest new perks
summary: The ESPN Unlimited upgrade is now complete.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR ESPN Unlimited is now fully integrated into YouTube TV. Eligible subscribers can watch its content without switching to the ESPN app. The integration also brings features like multiview, alternate feeds, and ESPN Fantasy support. YouTube TV and ESPN have been on a bit of a rollercoaster, with last year’s Disney carriage dispute briefly taking ESPN and other channels off the service. One of the sweeteners when the two sides eventually struck a new deal was access to ESPN Unlimited for YouTube TV subscribers, and that started rolling out in August . But until now, you still had to leave YouTube TV and watch it on the ESPN app. That changes today, with ESPN Unlimited now fully integrated into YouTube TV. YouTube announced the full integration in a blog post , confirming that it applies to subscribers on the main YouTube TV plan or any plan that includes Sports. That brings events including the US Open, college football, PGA Tour golf, WWE Premium Live Events, La Liga, and out-of-market NHL games into the app, along with ESPN Originals, Films, and the full 30 for 30 library.

title: Your Pixel 11 will soon have a fix for the static noise ruining your videos
summary: Google confirms Pixel 11 video static noise bug, promises a fix is coming.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel 11 series users have been reporting an issue with Video Boost. The issue causes static noise to appear in videos recorded with the feature. A Google spokesperson has confirmed to Android Authority that a fix has been identified and a rollout will come in the following weeks. The Pixel 11 series just recently launched, and it’s stumbling out of the gate with a video recording problem. If you’ve noticed noisy static in your recordings, you’re not alone. As Android Authority reported last week, a number of buyers have been experiencing this problem. Fortunately, it may not be long before a fix arrives. To quickly summarize the situation, we spotted reports on Reddit that suggested there was an issue with Video Boost (a Pixel camera feature that enhances video color, lighting, stabilization, and low-light detail). According to the reports, videos captured with this feature on contained static noise. The cause of the issue is unknown, but some attributed it to an Audio Zoom (a feature that boosts the sound of the zoomed-in subject while cutting down background noise) bug.

title: Take a look: Users are now getting Android’s convoluted sideloading process, and everyone hates it
summary: Android owners are getting Google's new sideloading process, and new screenshots give us an even closer look.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR At least one Android device owner has received the advanced flow for sideloading apps. The user shared screenshots outlining the process, covering the 24-hour wait and more. Fellow users expressed frustration with this change, while our own poll earlier this year also revealed widespread opposition. Google announced a couple of weeks ago that it had started rolling out its advanced flow for sideloading apps on Android devices. This controversial new process requires users to restart their phones and then wait 24 hours before they can sideload apps, and a user has shared screenshots of this new flow. Redditor Super-Ad8814 recently received the new sideloading flow on their unidentified Android device. A shared screenshot (see first image below) indeed shows that you need to confirm whether someone asked you to allow sideloading. This section also informs users that scammers often tell victims to sideload apps. Google’s fine print adds that government employees and legitimate business representatives will never ask you to enable sideloading.

title: Google’s new Extreme Charging on the Pixel 11 Pro XL has a heat problem
summary: Is being 5 minutes faster really worth the higher temperatures?
body: Getting the new Pixel 11 Pro XL to fast charge as quickly as Google claims is no easy feat. First, you need to grab yourself a 45W USB PD PPS charger that supports 21V for this specific protocol. Not a hugely tall order, but it might require buying a new charger, even if you have a relatively new PPS model that only supports 11V. Secondly, there’s a new option to toggle Google’s Extreme Charging capability, which promises to shave up to five minutes off your charging needs, but you’ll need some good fortune to get it to work. In a classic Google move, Extreme Charging isn’t available right out of the box. I still haven’t figured out the exact spell required to spring into life. In my experience, the Extreme Charging settings option appeared after charging the Pixel 11 Pro XL from empty to full twice and then simply waiting for it to show up. In any case, with the feature finally unlocked, I’ve been able to test the pros and cons of the latest Pixel’s boosted charging capabilities.

title: Apple’s first folding iPhone won’t kill Android foldables — it will save them
summary: Apple could finally make foldables cool.
body: We’re fast approaching a decade since the first commercially available foldable phones arrived — yes, I’m counting the hilariously bad Royole FlexPai. Yet, despite the strides we’ve made in the technology behind them, foldables as a category are stuck behind a proverbial wall. Everyone from Samsung to Google, Motorola, and a plethora of Chinese OEMs have spent years redesigning hinges, improving displays, and offering increasingly aggressive trade-in deals to spur take-up. Despite that, foldables still make up just 1.6% of global smartphone shipments.

The update appears to be a gradual server-side rollout, with some devices getting the refreshed UI before the translation feature arrives. For most of its existence, Gemini Live’s interface barely changed. That shifted in April when Google began testing a redesign that ditched the dedicated full-screen experience. Now, Google appears to be quietly refining that experience again, and the latest change could be much more useful than another visual refresh. A new “Turn on live translation” option appears to be rolling out to some users, enabling Gemini Live to translate conversations between languages in real time.
